name: Frosthaven
worldBackground: A rugged coastal hamlet where families eke out a living from the sea, its mood is one of quiet resilience and hard-won warmth. The villagers rely on the unpredictable tides and the mercy of the ocean, but tensions simmer beneath the surface—last winter’s storm took a fisherman’s life, and the widowed net-mender’s skills are both revered and resented. The inn, a rare beacon of hospitality, offers respite to weary travelers, though its owner’s sharp tongue keeps many at arm’s length.

rooms.name: Common Room
rooms.purpose: A wind-sheltered hall with a central hearth, where fishermen and travelers gather. The walls are lined with shelves holding lanterns, fishing tools, and preserved goods. A long wooden bar runs along the north wall, and tables with benches are scattered around.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.purpose: A functional cooking space with a large hearth, a wooden table for prep work, and shelves stocked with pots, pans, and preserved food. A barrel of fresh water sits near the door.

rooms.name: Guest Corridor
rooms.purpose: A narrow passage connecting the Common Room to the guest rooms and kitchen. Shelves line the walls, and lanterns provide light.

rooms.name: Guest Room
rooms.purpose: A modest room for travelers, furnished with a single bed, a small table, and a shelf for personal items. A lantern hangs near the door.

rooms.name: Main Storage
rooms.purpose: A cavernous space lined with weathered stone walls, housing nets, tools, and preserved fish. The air is damp and smells faintly of salt and brine. A single lantern hangs from a rafter, casting long shadows. A small hearth in one corner provides meager warmth, and a smokehouse occupies a far wall, its door slightly ajar. The floor is uneven, with wooden planks laid over the packed earth in high-traffic areas.

rooms.name: Tool Shed
rooms.purpose: A smaller, more organized space for tools and repair equipment. An anvil sits in the center, surrounded by coils of rope, hammers, and net-mending tools. Shelves line the walls, holding spare parts, twine, and patches. A wooden workbench runs along one wall, with a stool tucked beside it. The door to the Main Storage is visible through the open doorway.

npcs.name: Mirabel Harkness
npcs.description: A sharp-tongued woman who runs the inn with an iron fist, she wants the place to thrive but worries the villagers’ grudges will one day turn to fists.
npcs.physicalDescription: Stocky with salt-cracked hands, she wears a stained apron over a dark dress and keeps her iron-gray hair tied back in a tight knot, always ready for a brawl or a brawl’s aftermath.

npcs.name: Father Aldric Veyne
npcs.description: A gaunt, silver-haired man who tends to the spiritual needs of the villagers but secretly fears the sea’s wrath after losing his brother in a storm; he longs for a sign of divine favor to ease the village’s grief.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and lean, clad in a frayed brown robe, his hands are always stained with ink from recording births and deaths, and his eyes hold a quiet sorrow that never leaves.

npcs.name: Eamon Harkness
npcs.description: A broad-shouldered widower who mends nets with calloused hands, his only comfort the quiet rhythm of his work—though he secretly fears the sea will take another from his village, as it did his wife.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and lean, with salt-streaked dark hair tied back, he wears a patched woolen tunic and fingerless gloves, his left thumb permanently stained with tar from years of repair.

npcs.name: Martha Harkness
npcs.description: Eamon’s wife, now aged and frail, spends her days tending the hearth and weaving small repairs into the nets he brings home—her hands still steady, though her voice is often lost to the wind’s howl.
npcs.physicalDescription: Slender and silver-haired, she wears a thick shawl over a faded dress, her knuckles gnarled from years of stitching, and her eyes hold the quiet grief of a woman who lost her love to the same sea that sustains them.

npcs.name: Cedric Hale
npcs.description: A broad-shouldered fisherman with a quiet but stubborn streak, Cedric clings to the old ways of mending nets himself rather than rely on Eamon’s yard, though his pride may cost him when the next storm hits.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and barrel-chested, his face is permanently wind-chapped, and he wears a heavy wool tunic with a salt-stained leather belt.

npcs.name: Elspeth Hale
npcs.description: A sharp-eyed woman who keeps the household running, Elspeth secretly fears her husband’s rivalry with the net-mender will bring misfortune, but she’d never admit it aloud.
npcs.physicalDescription: Stocky and strong from years of hauling nets, her hands are rough, and she wears a dark apron over a simple wool dress, always pinned with a silver thimble.

npcs.name: Finn Hale
npcs.description: A wiry 12-year-old with a chip on his shoulder, Finn begs his father to let him sail, but Cedric refuses—until the day a storm traps them both at sea.
npcs.physicalDescription: Skinny and quick, his hair is perpetually tangled, and he wears a patched-up tunic with his father’s old fishing knife tucked into his belt.

npcs.name: Marnie Hale
npcs.description: A quiet 9-year-old who collects shells and whispers to the tide, Marnie believes the sea speaks to her—though her father calls it foolishness.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and delicate, her braids are often loose, and she wears a worn leather apron over her dress, always with a small pouch of shells at her belt.

npcs.name: Borin Bracken
npcs.description: A superstitious man who refuses to sail in storms, Borin blames the net-mender’s wife for his bad luck after her death, though he’d never dare say it to her face.
npcs.physicalDescription: Short and stocky, his face is round and flushed, and he wears a thick, hooded cloak even in the village, as if warding off bad omens.

npcs.name: Thora Bracken
npcs.description: A sharp-tongued woman who runs the household with an iron fist, Thora resents the Hales’ defiance of the net-mender and would love to see Cedric’s boat sink—if only to prove her husband right.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and lean, her dark hair is always pinned back, and she wears a high-collared dress with a silver brooch shaped like a fish.

npcs.name: Tessa Bracken
npcs.description: A bold 11-year-old with a taste for trouble, Tessa sneaks into the net-mender’s yard to spy on the villagers, convinced she’ll uncover a secret that will make her famous.
npcs.physicalDescription: Freckled and wiry, her clothes are always rumpled, and she wears a stolen fisherman’s cap too big for her head.

npcs.name: Garrick Marlow
npcs.description: A broad-shouldered man with calloused hands, Garrick is the elder Marlow son who shoulders his father’s duties after his death last winter; he fears the sea’s wrath but refuses to let his family starve.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and wind-lean, his salt-streaked beard is braided back, and his woolen tunic is patched at the elbows from years of hauling nets.

npcs.name: Liora Marlow
npcs.description: Liora keeps the cottage running with a steady hand, mending nets and preserving fish while secretly longing for a life beyond the docks—she dreams of her sister’s weaving guild in the next village.
npcs.physicalDescription: Her dark braid is always pinned with a silver thimble, and her apron is thick with flour and fish scales, her knuckles raw from stitching.

npcs.name: Riven Marlow
npcs.description: A wiry 12-year-old with a knack for knots, Riven mimics his father’s work but chafes at being called too young for the sea—he’s already carved a miniature boat from driftwood.
npcs.physicalDescription: His hair is perpetually tangled from wind and salt, and his fingers are always stained with ink from scribbling tally marks on scraps of parchment.

npcs.name: Sylvie Marlow
npcs.description: Sylvie, 9, is the cottage’s unofficial storyteller, weaving tales of mermaids and lost ships to distract from the storms—she fears the dark but never lets it show.
npcs.physicalDescription: Her dress is embroidered with tiny fish, and her eyes are always wide, as if listening for the next wave’s whisper.

npcs.name: Dain Durn
npcs.description: A grizzled veteran of the sea, Dain resents Garrick’s rise and whispers that the younger man’s luck is borrowed—he clings to old superstitions, like never casting off on a Tuesday.
npcs.physicalDescription: His face is a map of scars, and his cloak is lined with dried seaweed for luck, though he’d never admit it.

npcs.name: Hilda Durn
npcs.description: Hilda tends the cottage’s herb garden, brewing remedies for the village but secretly hoping her son will take the priest’s path—she fears the sea’s cruelty but dares not voice it.
npcs.physicalDescription: Her hands are always damp from washing, and her sleeves are rolled to the elbows, revealing bruises from Dain’s temper.

npcs.name: Orren Durn
npcs.description: A lanky 14-year-old with a talent for carving, Orren sells whittled fish to tourists but dreams of becoming a ship’s carpenter—he hides his sketches for fear his father will burn them.
npcs.physicalDescription: His hair is perpetually tousled, and his tunic is always dusted with wood shavings, his fingers stained with linseed oil.

player.name: Kaelan Veyne
player.role: an outsider with a reason to stay the season
player.description: A former scribe turned wandering scholar, Kaelan seeks to document the village’s folklore and lost maritime traditions before the next storm season cuts him off from the mainland.
player.physicalDescription: Lean and wind-burnished, clad in a patched woolen fisherman’s coat over a dark tunic, his left hand bears the faint scar of a ship’s rope burn—his only souvenir from a life at sea.

narrativeRules: Emphasize the gale’s howl and the creak of ropes—every sound is a reminder of the sea’s power and the village’s fragility.
Let tensions simmer: a sharp word over a shared net, a glance that lingers too long, or a child’s laughter cutting through the cold.
Storms are never just weather—they’re tests of skill, luck, and who the village will turn to (or against) when the waves rise.
The Net-Mender’s Yard is a place of both reverence and resentment; his tools are prized, but his presence is a thorn in some ribs.
Food and fuel are scarce but never free—every coin spent at the Old Salt Tavern is a story of trust (or debt) told over ale.
The Chapel’s bell tolls for more than the dead; it marks the hours, the tides, and the moments when the village must choose: to help or to hoard.
A lost fishing knife or a snapped line isn’t just broken—it’s a call to action, a chance to prove worth, or a spark for blame.
The Storehouse’s dust is a metaphor: supplies rot, trust decays, and the village’s survival depends on who steps forward to mend what’s broken.

currency.name: fisher’s mark
currency.description: a silver coin stamped with a herring, worth a day’s catch or a night’s lodging at the Old Salt Tavern

variables.name: Rumours
variables.value: The Net-Mender’s daughter was seen speaking to a stranger in the docks.
variables.initial: The Net-Mender’s daughter was seen speaking to a stranger in the docks.

lowZone.effectDesc: hunger pains and gnawing stomachs—some families ration their last meal.
The Net-Mender avoids your gaze; his tools are ‘unavailable’ when you need them.

highZone.effectDesc: The Net-Mender offers a free repair or a word of advice—his respect is a rare currency.

lowZone.effectDesc: The innkeeper serves your ale watered down and ignores your requests.

highZone.effectDesc: The innkeeper offers you a free meal or a bed—your word carries weight.

lowZone.effectDesc: Whispers follow you; offers of help turn to cold shoulders.

highZone.effectDesc: Families share their catch or lend tools without hesitation.

root.name: Stranger’s Hands
root.description: Your outsider status means villagers tolerate you but do not trust you. You gain a +1 to Persuasion checks when dealing with locals, but you cannot assume favors or shelter without earning them first.
root.physicalDescription: A pair of rough, uncalloused hands gripping a wooden oar.

children.name: Net-Mender’s Apprentice
children.description: Spend 3 hours assisting Eamon Harkness in his yard, and he will teach you one basic knot or repair technique. Once per season, you may attempt a check to mend a net or rope without penalty.
children.physicalDescription: A neatly tied square knot in a frayed rope.

children.name: Martha’s Trust
children.description: Martha Harkness begins to share meals with you during storms. Once per season, she may reveal a family secret or a hidden grievance within the village if you’ve helped her husband.
children.physicalDescription: A steaming bowl of fish stew passed through an open cottage door.

children.name: Storm-Watcher’s Instinct
children.description: Eamon teaches you to read the sea’s signs. Once per week, attempt a check to predict mild weather changes (e.g., incoming fog or light rain). Success grants a +1 to Survival checks for the next 24 hours.
children.physicalDescription: A crow’s foot pattern carved into a wooden paddle.

children.name: Fisher’s Apprentice
children.description: A fishing family invites you to join their next trip if you assist them for a full day. Gain a +1 to Survival checks related to fishing for the season, and you may attempt to catch one extra fish per trip.
children.physicalDescription: A wooden bucket half-filled with glistening herring.

children.name: The Family’s Mark
children.description: The family you apprenticed under will offer you a place to stay during storms or share a meal if you’ve helped them. Once per season, they may grant you a small favor, like delivering a message or mending gear.
children.physicalDescription: A handshake over a shared meal of salted herring.

root.name: Unyielding Will
root.description: You endure Frosthaven’s hardships without complaint. Gain a +1 to Endurance checks in harsh weather, and you may attempt one additional check per day to push through fatigue.
root.physicalDescription: A lone figure standing against a howling wind, chin raised.

children.name: Storm’s Lesson
children.description: Survive a severe storm without taking damage, and gain a temporary +2 to Endurance checks for 24 hours. Villagers who witness your resilience may treat you with slight respect afterward.
children.physicalDescription: A shipwrecked mast half-buried in sand, scarred by salt.

children.name: Beacon of Hope
children.description: Once per season, a villager in distress may turn to you for help, knowing you’ve faced storms before. They will offer a reward—whether a favor, a meal, or information—if you assist them.
children.physicalDescription: A flickering lantern in a cottage window during a storm.

children.name: Cold’s Embrace
children.description: You’re accustomed to the cold. Gain a +1 to Endurance checks in freezing conditions, and ignore minor cold-related penalties (e.g., slowed movement).
children.physicalDescription: A breath of frost curling around a figure’s face.

children.name: Frost’s Grip
children.description: Endure a night of extreme cold without damage, and gain a +2 to Endurance checks for 48 hours. You may also warm another person by sharing body heat, granting them a +1 to Endurance for one hour.
children.physicalDescription: Hands wrapped around a steaming mug of hot cider.

children.name: Wind’s Song
children.description: Attempt a check to interpret the wind’s direction or strength once per week. Success grants a +1 to Survival checks for navigation or weather prediction for 24 hours.
children.physicalDescription: A feather caught in the wind, spinning lazily above the docks.

children.name: Sailor’s Whisper
children.description: Fishermen may ask for your counsel before sailing. If you succeed on a check, they’ll follow your advice, improving their chances of safe passage.
children.physicalDescription: A hand pointing toward the horizon, where the wind carries distant shores.

root.name: Familiar Face
root.description: Villagers no longer ignore you. Gain a +1 to Persuasion and Insight checks, and attempt one additional check per day to earn trust or uncover secrets.
root.physicalDescription: A figure standing at the center of the Village Green, surrounded by villagers.

children.name: Chapel’s Welcome
children.description: Attend a service or help at the chapel, and Father Aldric will invite you to share a meal. Once per season, he may reveal a moral dilemma or offer a blessing granting a +1 to one check.
children.physicalDescription: A wooden cross hanging above the chapel door.

children.name: Confessor’s Trust
children.description: Once per season, a villager may seek your counsel. Offer advice based on their struggles, and if heeded, they may grant you a favor.
children.physicalDescription: Hands clasped in prayer, symbolizing trust.

children.name: Family’s Bond
children.description: Spend a full day with a fishing family, and they’ll invite you to join their celebrations. Once per season, you may call upon them for aid, though they may expect something in return.
children.physicalDescription: A shared meal around a crackling fire.

children.name: Heir’s Promise
children.description: A child may ask for your help once per season. Succeed in assisting them, and they may reveal a secret or hidden truth about the village.
children.physicalDescription: A child’s hand in yours, eyes wide with trust.

children.name: Tavern’s Keeper
children.description: Mirabel offers you discounts or meals if you’ve helped her. Once per season, she may reveal a secret or gossip that could be useful.
children.physicalDescription: A tankard raised in toast, the tavern’s warmth enveloping you.

children.name: Innkeeper’s Confidant
children.description: Once per season, Mirabel may reveal a secret about a villager or stranger. Use this information to earn favors, avoid danger, or uncover hidden truths.
children.physicalDescription: A whispered conversation in the tavern’s corner.

calendar.name: Net-Mending Lesson
calendar.missedConsequence: Eamon Harkness will not trust you with his craft, and the villagers will whisper that you lack the skills to contribute to their survival. You’ll be seen as a burden, and the door to the Old Salt Tavern will stay closed to you for the season.

calendar.name: Storm Warning Gathering
calendar.missedConsequence: The villagers will assume you’re unprepared for the harsh realities of Frosthaven. You’ll be excluded from the storm preparations, and your reputation as an outsider will deepen—no one will share supplies or shelter with you if the winds pick up.

calendar.name: Herring Fishery Shift
calendar.missedConsequence: The fishermen will see you as unreliable. Cedric Hale will refuse to let you join their crew next time, and you’ll miss out on a chance to earn their trust—or their coin.

calendar.name: Chapel Service
calendar.missedConsequence: Father Aldric will note your absence, and the villagers will assume you lack respect for their traditions. You’ll be seen as an outsider who doesn’t belong, and your path to integration will grow steeper.

calendar.name: Tide-Timing Drill
calendar.missedConsequence: The fishermen will mock your lack of knowledge about the tides. Borin Bracken will refuse to teach you anything further, and you’ll struggle to prove your worth in the village.

objectives.text: Help Eamon Harkness mend the storm-damaged nets for the village’s fishing fleet by the end of the week.

prerequisites.text: Learn the basics of net-mending from Eamon in Net-Mender’s Yard (day 0, 09:00–11:00).
Assist Cedric Hale in repairing his personal fishing gear at the Harbor Docks (day 1, 14:00–16:00).

objectives.text: Prove your worth to the villagers by participating in at least two fishing shifts or storm preparations before the next full moon.

prerequisites.text: Join the herring fishery shift on day 3 (05:00–11:00) at the Harbor Docks.
Attend the Storm Warning Gathering on day 2 (16:00) at the Village Green and offer to help with preparations.

objectives.text: Gain Father Aldric’s blessing by attending the Chapel Service on day 4 (10:00) and speaking with him afterward.

prerequisites.text: Attend the Chapel Service on day 4 (10:00–11:00) at the Village Chapel.
Bring a small offering (e.g., a fish caught during your shift) to the Chapel by day 5.

quests.title: Uncover the Truth Behind Last Winter’s Storm

objectives.text: Speak with Martha Harkness at Net-Mender’s Cottage to learn more about her late husband’s final days.

prerequisites.text: Visit Martha Harkness at Net-Mender’s Cottage on day 1 or 2 (after 12:00).

objectives.text: Investigate the old fishing logs stored in the Fishermen’s Storehouse to find records of unusual weather patterns.

prerequisites.text: Gain access to the Fishermen’s Storehouse by asking Garrick Marlow for the key (day 2, 10:00–12:00).

objectives.text: Confront Borin Bracken at the Harbor Docks about rumors of his involvement in last winter’s tragedy.

prerequisites.text: Find Borin Bracken at the Harbor Docks on day 5 or 6 (before 14:00).
